## Create and select columns

In this milestone, you'll write some of the code that was written for you in milestone 2. This will familiarize you with the format of the events data.

In the chunk below the events_formatted.parquet file is read in, named "events", and filtered for health events. You can just add your code to this chunk in order to acomplish the tasks listed below the chunk.

You will recognize select helper functions like starts_with() and contains(). These are used to simplify your data so there are not so many columns to look at.

This data comes from a dairy comp report events/2 with several additional options and switches.

```{r}
events<-read_parquet(here::here('data/intermediate_files/events_formatted.parquet'))%>%
   select(location_event, 
         id_animal, 
         id_animal_lact,
         id, date_birth,
         lact_number, lact_group,
         event_type, date_event,
         dim_event, dop_event, starts_with('age'), 
          event, remark, protocols, locate_lesion,
         contains('event'), 
         contains('remark'), 
         contains('protocols') 
         )%>%
  filter(event_type %in% 'health',event %in% c("MAST","LAME"),lact_number>0) |>
  fxn_add_event_counts() |>
  mutate(
    category_dop_event = case_when(
      dop_event>0 & dop_event<=100        ~ "Early Lactation",
      dop_event>100 & dop_event<=200      ~ "Mid Lactation",
      dop_event>200                       ~ "Late Lactation"
      ),
    #) |>
    #  mutate(
      floordate_year=floor_date(date_event,"year")
      )
  #events$floordate_month_test<-floor_date(events$date_event,"months")
#I can mutate above variables separately or in one move using pipes. If I want to do the dangerous way without pipes and MODIFY the original data set I can use the $ line of code at 66.
event_counts_by_month<-events |>
  distinct(id_animal,event,floordate_month,category_dop_event)

 #?floor_date
#This can be used for a TON of date and time rounding, etc. More to come in other milestones
```

1.  add a pipe to filter `events` further so you only have only one or 2 unique health events that are interesting to you. The example in the solution is based on 'NAVEL' and 'SEPTIC' events, but choose anything you want. If it is not NAVEL and SEPTIC don't worry about the solutions not matching in this milestone.

2.  add a pipe to create a new variable named **floordate_month**. The logic to create this variable is: **floor_date(date_event, 'months')**

3.  add a pipe to the function fxn_add_event_counts(). This will add columns indicating the number of times the animal has had that event within the data set (event_count_animal) or within their lactation (event_count_lact). If you would like to see the code the creates these click on the function in your environment. Look at the data frame an check to see that the values in the new variables of event_count_animal and event_count_lact make sense. (hint: an easy way to do this is to look at a dataframe of only 1 animal and arrange it properly).  Are these counts logical?

4.  add a pipe and use mutate to create a new variable named `category_dop_event`.  This new variable should categorize the day of phase at the time of the event (dop_event). Your new variable should allow you to look at specific dop intervals for the event you are interested in. The cut points should be sensical based on your questions about the event you picked. If you prefer to use dim_event or age_event that is fine.

5. Create a new dataframe that uses the distinct() function to count the number of unique animals (id_animal) within each event and floordate_month, and category_dop_event.  Name this dataframe `event_counts_by_month`.

### Step 2 - Disease and Treatments

Look at the example graphic below the next chunk. Pay special attention to the x axis as well as the facet and fill variables.

Create 2 new variables for your events named: `Disease` and `Treatment`. Use case_when() and whichever columns you would like to create the most useful variables.  Notice that there are several options for columns that contain the information from Remark. Explore them and see if any are useful for your events.

Run the chunk below to see the example graphics. . . . your graphics can be prettier!

```{r}
#starting "small" with just mastitise event data

events |>
  mutate(
    # Count how many of the 4 unique patterns appear in the string
    quarter_count = str_count(locate_lesion, "LR|RR|LF|RF"),

    Disease_QQ_count = case_when(
      is.na(locate_lesion)          ~ "No Quarter Recorded",
      quarter_count == 1            ~ "Only One Affected",
      quarter_count == 2            ~ "Two Affected",
      quarter_count == 3            ~ "Three Affected",
      quarter_count == 4            ~ "All Four Affected",
      .default                      = "Check Data"
      ),
      #Must put the ONLY category first, then the AFFECTED second since R reads and looks for the first condition. If I write affected first, then the only category gets "lost" in the affected column as well. If I put >1 then I am removing all "only" counts from the total for affected (not overlapping). Might make more sense to write > vs >= for clarity and just add the two (only + affected = ALL LEFT REAR CASES, etc).
    Disease_QQ_Category1 = case_when( 
      str_detect(locate_lesion,"LR") & quarter_count==1                        ~ "Left Rear Only",
      str_detect(locate_lesion,"RR") & quarter_count==1                        ~ "Right Rear Only",
      str_detect(locate_lesion,"LF") & quarter_count==1                        ~ "Left Front Only",
      str_detect(locate_lesion,"RF") & quarter_count==1                        ~ "Right Front Only",
      str_detect(locate_lesion,"LR") & quarter_count>1                        ~ "Left Rear Included",
      str_detect(locate_lesion,"RR") & quarter_count>1                        ~ "Right Rear Included",
      str_detect(locate_lesion,"LF") & quarter_count>1                        ~ "Left Front Included",
      str_detect(locate_lesion,"RF") & quarter_count>1                        ~ "Right Front Included",
      .default                      = "Check Data"
      ),
    Disease_QQ_Category1Total = case_when(
      Disease_QQ_Category1 %in% ("Left Rear Only","Left Rear Included")   ~"Left Rear Total",
      Disease_QQ_Category1 %in% ("Right Rear Only","Right Rear Included")   ~"Right Rear Total",
      Disease_QQ_Category1 %in% ("Left Front Only","Left Front Included")   ~"Left Front Total",
      Disease_QQ_Category1 %in% ("Right Front Only","Right Front Included")   ~"Right Front Total",
      .default                      = "Check Data"
    ),
    Disease_QQ_Category2 =case_when(
      str_detect(locate_lesion,"LF") & str_detect(locate_lesion,"RF") & quarter_count==2          ~ "Both Front",
      str_detect(locate_lesion,"LR") & str_detect(locate_lesion,"RR") & quarter_count==2          ~ "Both Rear",
      str_detect(locate_lesion,"LF") & str_detect(locate_lesion,"LR") & quarter_count==2          ~ "Both Left",
      str_detect(locate_lesion,"RF") & str_detect(locate_lesion,"RR") & quarter_count==2          ~ "Both Right",
      .default="Check Data"
    ),
    Treatment = case_when(
      remark_letters1=="NOT"                         ~ "No Treatment",
      remark_letters1=="TOD"                         ~ "Today IMM",
      remark_letters1=="SPC"                         ~ "SpectraMast LC IMM",
      remark_letters1=="AMX"                         ~ "AmoxiMast IMM",
      locate_lesion=="LR"                         ~ "Killed Quarter",
    )
    )

    #Disease = case_when(
    #  locate_lesion=="LR"                         ~ "Left Rear Only",
     # locate_lesion>="LR"                         ~ "Left Rear Affected",
    #  locate_lesion=="RR"                         ~ "Right Rear Only",
     # locate_lesion>="RR"                         ~ "Right Rear Affected",
    #  locate_lesion=="LF"                         ~ "Left Front Only",
    #  locate_lesion>="LF"                         ~ "Left Front Affected",
   #   locate_lesion=="RF"                         ~ "Right Front Only",
   #   locate_lesion>="RF"                         ~ "Right Front Affected",
   #   is.na(locate_lesion)                         ~ "No Quarter Recorded",
    #  locate_lesion %in% c("LR","RR","LF","RF")                 ~ "Only One Affected",
      #locate_lesion                           ~ "Two Affected",
      #locate_lesion %in% c()                              ~ "Three Affected",
```

Then use graphs, tables, or a combination to describe your selected events.  Has there has been a change in the treatments used over time?  Does dop (day of phase i.e. dim or age) matter for your selected events?

CAUTION: do not over think this.  I know you are all wanting to do this with a denominator to find incidence rather than raw counts.  I promise that is coming. First just get used to summarizing numerators across different groupings. 

Note: your graphics should be much prettier than the examples!! ;)



```{r}
#graph your event counts over time here.

MASTLAMEbyLactPhaseSummary<-event_counts_by_month |>
  group_by(event, floordate_month, category_dop_event) |>
  summarize(
    n_event=n(),
    n_distinct_id_event=n_distinct(id_animal),
    min_count_MAST=min()
    avg_count_MAST
    max_count_MAST
    min_count_LAME
    avg_count_LAME
    max_count_LAME
  )


MASTLAMEByLactPhaseGraph1<-
  ggplot(
    data=event_counts_by_month,
    mapping=aes(x=event)
  ) +
    geom_bar()

MASTLAMEByLactPhaseGraph1

```
